title: Composable hosted endpoints PRD, governance rules, and go‑live checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for a composable hosted endpoint model that lets product teams assemble chat, completions, embeddings and rerank capabilities via reusable sub-resources. Includes governance and launch readiness checklist to ensure backwards compatibility, quota behavior, and observability before GA.
problem_statement: Current hosted endpoints are siloed by capability and require duplicated config for auth, routing, and monitoring. Customers building multi-capability flows face inconsistent semantic guarantees across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank and higher onboarding friction. We need a modular surface that reduces duplication, enforces consistent defaults, and provides a clear migration path.
goals: Deliver a single composable endpoint model that can host chat, completion, embedding, and rerank operations under a unified contract
Preserve backwards compatibility for existing hosted API consumers (no breaking changes at GA)
Provide governance defaults: rate limiting, model fallback policy, and tenant-level quotas
Ship a prescriptive launch checklist with observability, docs, SDK examples, and migration guidance
Enable customers to opt into per-route performance profiles (low-latency vs cost-optimized)
success_metrics: <10% integration bugs reported in first 30 days after GA
<1% latency regression vs existing endpoint baseline for P95 on standard chat workloads
>60% of new hosted customers adopt composable endpoint for multi-capability flows within 90 days
Complete security review and SOC readiness sign-off before GA
out_of_scope: Dedicated capacity features (reserved GPU pools) — those will be mapped to the composable surface in a later phase
On-prem/Private deployment packaging changes — kept for Private roadmap
Major SDK rewrites; SDK additions will be additive shims for migration
technical_requirements: One stable URL pattern for composable endpoint: /v1/endpoint/{endpoint_id} supporting operation subtypes
Explicit operation type field in payload (chat|completion|embedding|rerank) with validation
Preserve existing API contracts for legacy endpoints via compatibility aliasing and routing rules
Request-level policy evaluation for model routing and fallback (latency-first, cost-first, pinned)
Quota and rate-limit enforcement at tenant and endpoint levels with clear headers for remaining tokens/calls
Streaming support for chat and completions with same SSE/HTTP chunk semantics as current hosted API
Prefix KV caching must be compatible with composable session semantics and expose cache hit/miss metrics
api_surface: POST /v1/endpoint/{id} - main entrypoint; body includes 'operation' and 'input' fields
Query params: streaming=true to enable chunked responses
Accepts 'model' (optional), 'profile' (low-latency|balanced|cost-optimized), and per-request hints for reranking (score_metric)
Response shapes: mirrors existing operation outputs; compat mode headers set when request routed to legacy handler
Error codes: extend existing error taxonomy with OPERATION_MISMATCH, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED
auth_and_security: Existing API key model continues to work; new endpoint honors key scoping and rate quotas
Add support for scoped service tokens to grant limited write/exec rights to composed sub-resources
Audit log entries for operation type, model chosen, fallback decisions, and tenant_id must be emitted
Security review required for KMS/KVS interactions used by prefix caching and session storage
observability_and_monitoring: Per-operation telemetry: request_count, success_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_count
Expose model-choice distribution and fallback rates for each endpoint in Console
Cost breakdown per route and per operation in usage analytics (tokens vs compute)
Tracing hooks to correlate across sub-requests when composable flows fan-out to multiple model calls
Alerting rules: fallback_rate > 3% sustained over 10m, P95 latency > baseline + 20%
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: internal users + 5 partners; feature-flagged by tenant; monitor metrics for 72h
Phase 1 - Early access: opt-in for customers via Console toggle; 2 week soak with expanded traffic
Phase 2 - Gradual GA: rollout traffic ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with automated rollback on SLO breaches
Migration guidance: legacy endpoints will remain active and route to composable handlers; provide deprecation timeline only if no regressions
launch_checklist: API contract doc published with examples for chat/completion/embedding/rerank
SDK shims for JavaScript and Python released with migration samples
Console: per-endpoint settings UI and billing preview exists
Quota and rate-limiter instrumented and validated under load
Security review completed and KMS integration validated
E2E perf tests executed comparing composable vs legacy endpoints on representative workloads
Canary customers identified and partner comms drafted
Runbook for common failures (model unavailable, quota errors, streaming disconnects) added to ops playbook
Docs and migration guide published including code snippets and troubleshooting section
SLOs and alerting rules are live in production monitoring dashboards
acceptance_criteria: API compatibility: All legacy endpoints' canonical examples return identical outputs when routed through the composable surface (minor header differences allowed).
Performance: P95 latency for standard chat workload must be within 20% of legacy baseline under production-like load
Reliability: No data-plane errors introduced by composable layer in canary; error budget burn rate unchanged or improved
Governance: Tenant-level quota enforcement verified with automated tests and manual sampling
Observability: Console shows per-endpoint metrics and fallback rates; trace correlations are present for fan-out flows
Security: Audit logs capture operation_type and model decisions; security review sign-off documented
dependencies: ENG-23140 - runtime: model fallback policy implementation
ENG-23988 - infra: quota and rate-limiter changes
SEC-19 - security review and KMS test harness
risks: Behavioral divergence: subtle differences in decoding/temperature defaults could change customer outputs
Operational complexity: increased routing logic may add failure modes if not fully exercised in CI
Migration confusion: customers may unintentionally adopt new defaults leading to quality regressions
Performance regressions under high-concurrency due to new policy evaluation path
notes: We decided to keep 'model' optional in the request to preserve current developer ergonomics; profile hints will be used by routing policy.
PM/Eng pairing sessions scheduled weekly through rollout; next milestone is canary sign-off on 2026-03-10.
Design suggested explicit visual affordances in Console to indicate when an endpoint is in 'compatibility mode'.
